title: ESMO: Lilly touts 79% ADC response rate in competitive ovarian cancer space
summary: Eli Lilly has shared phase 1 data on an antibody-drug conjugate in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer, shedding light on the company’s chances of competing for a market targeted by rivals including AbbVie and Genmab.

title: ESMO: GSK cancer R&D chief says mo-rez data ‘reinforces our belief’ in ADC as phase 3 push ramps up
summary: GSK’s cancer R&D chief has suggested the latest slice of early-stage data on its B7-H4-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) has “reinforce[d] our belief in the asset,” as the therapy races through a clutch of phase 3 studies.

title: Roche puts numbers behind phase 3 kidney disease win amid blockbuster ambitions
summary: Roche's Genentech has put numbers behind its phase 3 success in IgA nephropathy (IgAN), reporting that antisense oligonucleotide sefaxersen reduced a key marker of kidney damage by 43.1% compared with placebo.

title: ESMO: Boehringer builds case for late-phase rival to Amgen’s Imdelltra
summary: Boehringer Ingelheim has shared data on its DLL3xCD3 T-cell engager, providing pointers to the prospects of a would-be rival to Amgen’s Imdelltra that entered phase 3 this year.

title: ESMO: Zentalis already dreaming of launch for WEE1 inhibitor after ‘great result’ in early-stage test
summary: Zentalis Pharmaceuticals has pointed to the first overall survival (OS) analysis for azenosertib as proof that the oral WEE1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor can offer a convenient oral treatment for a tricky cancer.

title: EQT buys molecular diagnostics specialist Qiagen in a €10.8B deal
summary: EQT is buying up Netherlands-based Qiagen in a deal worth €10.8 billion ($12.1 billion) in enterprise value that includes $1.1 billion in net debt.

title: ESMO: Takeda’s $1.2B bet on Innovent ‘absolutely’ pays off with details of ADC’s phase 3 win
summary: Takeda has lifted the lid on the phase 3 win for its next-generation claudin18.2 drug, with the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) demonstrating overall survival of 10.2 months.

title: Gilead to pay $1.3B upfront for PepStar’s oral IL-23 challenger to J&J’s Icotyde
summary: Gilead has struck a deal to acquire PepStar Therapeutics’ oral IL-23 receptor inhibitor program for $1.275 billion, positioning itself as a would-be challenger to Johnson & Johnson’s Icotyde across a range of inflammatory diseases.

title: Bolt makes inflammation play with Prana reverse merger, $120M financing
summary: Bolt Biotherapeutics is acquiring Prana Therapies in a stock-for-stock reverse merger backed by a $120 million financing to advance Prana’s lead antibody through multiple phase 2 trials in inflammatory diseases.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Troubled CSL enlists GSK vet Deborah Waterhouse to lead
summary: CSL has tapped a new leader to steer it through a make-or-break period. Ironwood's CEO since 2021 is hanging up his hat. CytoDyn's new helmsman is highlighting the company's "transformational period." And more.

title: BMS leads Pathos AI's $237M series E alongside Alzheimer's link-up
summary: Pathos AI has closed a $237 million series E round led by pharma giant Bristol Myers Squibb on the same day that the two companies signed a cutting-edge Alzheimer's disease-focused collaboration.

title: Roche pays Zymeworks $55M for trispecific challenger to Amgen’s Imdelltra
summary: Roche is paying Zymeworks $55 million upfront for ZW209, bagging global rights to a trispecific designed to improve on the rate and depth of responses achieved by Amgen’s Imdelltra.

title: Treasury sweeps biotech into proposed COINS Act restrictions, but spares Big Pharma’s China licensing deals
summary: Despite the sweeping scope of the ban covering various types of drug molecules, biopharma business development teams can breathe a measured sigh of relief.

title: ESMO: After leak, Merck and Moderna post phase 3 cancer vaccine data early
summary: Merck & Co. and Moderna have shared highly anticipated phase 3 data on their cancer vaccine ahead of schedule, revealing a primary endpoint hit that approached analysts’ best-case scenario. But the positive result was offset by weaker-than-expected data on a key secondary endpoint.

title: Menarini's Stemline picks up Georgiamune preclinical cancer immunotherapy in $1.1B deal
summary: Georgiamune, an immunology-focused biotech out of Maryland, has licensed a preclinical cancer drug candidate to Stemline Therapeutics, owned by Italy's Menarini Group, for up to $1.1 billion.

title: AbbVie scratches out phase 3 hidradenitis suppurativa win but falls short of expectations
summary: A phase 3 trial of AbbVie’s lutikizumab in hidradenitis suppurativa has hit its primary endpoint. But with the drug candidate beating placebo by a narrower margin than expected, the readout raises questions about AbbVie’s chances of cracking a competitive market.

title: Celltrion picks up another Kaigene autoimmune antibody for up to $580.5M
summary: Celltrion has licensed a preclinical antibody targeting autoimmune conditions from Maryland-based biotech Kaigene in a deal worth up to $580.5 million, marking another step in the South Korean drugmaker's expansion beyond its traditional biosimilar business.

title: Abbott to separate Nutrition business into an independent, publicly traded company
summary: Abbott will separate its Nutrition business into an independent, publicly traded company through a tax-free distribution to Abbott shareholders.

title: Quest Diagnostics’ test results system breached in yet another medtech cyberattack
summary: Quest Diagnostics is the latest life sciences company to fall victim to a cyberattack, with the company believing patient records have been compromised.

title: Rebranded NodThera plans IPO to fund NLRP3 inhibitor’s push toward approval
summary: NodThera—under its new name Rezera—is planning an IPO as the biotech steps up its ambitions to get its NLRP3 inhibitor to market.

title: Roche’s CEO has ‘absolutely not’ changed tune on Poseida despite scrapping CAR-T from the buyout
summary: Roche’s CEO has insisted to Fierce that the company’s view on its $1.5 billion Poseida buyout has “absolutely not” changed, even as the Swiss pharma scraps one of the CAR-T therapy’s from the acquisition.

title: ‘A two-way conversation with the tumor’: Researchers use ‘avatar’ to predict immunotherapy responses
summary: Researchers have explored a revolutionary way to predict a patient's response to immunotherapies by creating a tumor “avatar” from biopsies.

title: Amid bepirovirsen triumph, GSK quietly scraps trial of next-gen hep B therapy
summary: GSK may have cemented its hepatitis B credentials with Tuesday’s landmark FDA nod for its “functional cure” bepirovirsen, but the pharma continues to rethink its strategy for next-gen candidates.

title: Roche builds blockbuster BTK case for fenebrutinib in multiple sclerosis as FDA decision approaches
summary: Roche has dived into the data behind its filing for FDA approval of fenebrutinib in multiple sclerosis, unpacking the BTK inhibitor’s effect on chronic active lesions, disease control and brain volume.

title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02466-yThe authors developed methods to identify extracellular vesicles (EVs) in the blood that come from the brain by capturing EV surface proteins. This could be used in the future to diagnose neurological diseases.

title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin signaling
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02497-5This study shows that the sustained antidepressant-like effect of psychedelics is driven by 5-HT2A receptor–β-arrestin signaling. Repeated low-dose LSD preserves this effect in mice without inducing hallucinogenic-like behaviors in mice or monkeys.

title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02486-8The dimensionality of intrinsic brain connectivity systematically shapes how task representations compress and expand across the cortex, and activity flow modeling shows the active role of network geometry in generating the transformation.

title: Behavioral genomics identifies Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02484-wJiang et al. developed a robust postnatal knockout platform for somatosensory genomics and behavioral screening, identifying Creld1 as a cross-modal regulator of somatosensation through its control of sensory neuron excitability via voltage-gated sodium channels.

title: A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02458-yTang, Wu et al. identify a brain circuit that enables mother mice to wake selectively to pup cries. Motherhood strengthens this pathway through increased dopamine receptor D1 expression, helping mothers to be responsive to offspring during sleep.

title: SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02469-9SIK3 kinase controls synaptic NMDA receptor recruitment by phosphorylating GluN1 at a single site. Loss or inhibition of SIK3 markedly reduces synaptic NMDARs, while a gain-of-function mutation increases GluN1 phosphorylation and NMDAR levels.

title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s disease
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02487-7This study identifies ABCA1 as a driver of dysregulated cholesterol trafficking in Parkinson’s disease, showing that reducing ABCA1 in astrocytes and neurons decreases cholesterol accumulation, α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration in mice.

title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02485-9Sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus arise from two early-diverging lineages, with sensory neurons progressing through shared intermediate states, revealing how thalamic organization emerges during development.

title: Psilocybin Replaces Lost Synapses in Depressed Brains
summary: Does healing the brain with psychedelics require a "trip"? A new study shows psilocybin drives synaptic plasticity through Layer 5 pyramidal neurons independently of hallucinogenic signaling, opening the door to non-hallucinogenic depression therapeutics.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, depression, mental health, neurobiology, psilocybin, psychedelics, psychopharmacology, synapses, UC Santa Cruz

title: Neural Chip Powers Adaptive DBS for Depression
summary: Treating psychiatric illnesses with deep brain stimulation requires tracking multi-region brain networks. EPFL researchers developed LogSync, an ultra-low-power system-on-chip operating under 200 microwatts that decodes oscillatory synchrony to deliver real-time, responsive neuromodulation.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, DBS, deep-brain stimulation, depression, EPFL, mental health, neurobiology, Neurotech

title: Genetic Blueprint of Personality Revealed
summary: There is no single gene for being outgoing or anxious. A landmark Nature study of more than one million people identifies 1,260 genetic variants shaping the Big Five personality traits, showing that thousands of tiny DNA differences combine with environmental life experiences to mold human character.
category: Featured, Genetics, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, neurobiology, personality, University of Pennsylvania

title: Ultra-Processed Foods Sensitize Children’s Brain Reward Circuits
summary: Ultra-processed foods may condition developing brains to overeat. A longitudinal fMRI study in JAMA Network Open shows that high UPF intake sensitizes children's dorsal striatum to appetizing food images, directly driving body fat and BMI increases one year later.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain development, brain research, cognition, diet, neurobiology, neurodevelopment, ultraprocessed food, USC

title: How the Brain Maps Every Number
summary: How does the human brain process abstract mathematical values? Brain scans from the INSERM-CEA Cognitive Neuroimaging Unit reveal a continuous spatial map in the intraparietal sulcus that plots fractions and whole integers along a single mental number line.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, fMRI, intraparietal sulcus, math, Mathematical Cognition, neurobiology, Number Line, PLOS

title: Non-Drug Breakthrough for Postpartum Depression
summary: A free, self-paced online program developed by CU Boulder and Mass General researchers reduces postpartum depression relapse by 26%. The nationwide trial of 500 expectant mothers in Lancet Public Health provides a proven digital alternative to medication for preventing maternal mental health crises.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, depression, mental health, neurobiology, Neurotech, postpartum depression, PPD, University of Colorado

title: Cancer Drug Halts Fragile Brain Bleeds
summary: Cerebral Cavernous Malformation causes fragile, bleeding vascular lesions in the brain with no non-surgical treatment options. Researchers discovered that dabrafenib, an approved childhood cancer drug, suppresses vessel leakage and shrinks lesions in preclinical models.
category: Brain Cancer, Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, brain research, Cancer, cerebral cavernous malformation, neurobiology, neuropharmacology, Uppsala University

title: Astrocyte Subtypes Drive Synapse Formation and Memory
summary: Astrocytes are not a uniform support crew. A breakthrough study in Nature reveals that CD51-positive astrocyte subtypes specialize in building synapses via glypican 6, tuning hippocampal memory circuits, and repairing damaged connections after a stroke.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, astrocytes, Baylor College of Medicine, brain research, CD51+ astrocytes, glial cells, Memory, neurobiology, stroke, synapses

title: Restoring Brain Growth in Angelman Syndrome
summary: Angelman syndrome stems from a missing maternal UBE3A gene, but how it disrupts brain growth has remained unclear. Researchers at WashU Medicine discovered that accumulating asparagine synthetase tricks neurons into a perpetual emergency stress state, halting development. Blocking the enzyme restored normal brain growth in mice.
category: Featured, Genetics, Neurology, Neuroscience, Angelman Syndrome, brain development, brain research, developmental neuroscience, neurobiology, neurodevelopment, WUSTL

title: Conversational AI Is Cracking the Neuroimaging Bottleneck
summary: Turning raw brain scans into diagnostic discoveries currently requires weeks of complex computing across fragmented tools. A new $2.8M NIH-funded platform called UniBrain unites the entire neuroimaging pipeline into a single, conversational AI system.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, AI, Artificial Intelligence, brain research, Lehigh University, neurobiology, neuroimaging, Neurotech

title: Why AI Cannot Replace the Transformative Power of Human Creativity
summary: Generative AI can create masterpieces in seconds, but a new analysis reveals it breaks the crucial link between making art and personal growth. Hebrew University's Amit Zoran argues that the future of creativity belongs to human discovery and perspective rather than automated digital output.
category: Featured, Neurology, AI, Artificial Intelligence, brain research, creativity, Deep Learning, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Machine Learning, neurobiology, Neuroscience

title: Macrophages Settle in the Brain After Sepsis, Driving Memory Loss
summary: Surviving sepsis often leaves patients with lasting memory deficits. Researchers discovered that peripheral macrophages infiltrate the hippocampus during acute infection, establish lifelong residency, and signal microglia to devour protective myelin.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, brain research, cognition, macrophages, Memory, memory loss, neurobiology, sepsis
